primary_source: Released Fluent state; Ansys Fluent 26.1 User's Guide boundary-condition formulation; Ansys Fluent 26.1 Theory Guide section 4.7.4
source_detail: The saved SST/Transition SST setup uses Intensity and Viscosity Ratio specification with mu_t/mu = 10. Fluent documents 10 as the default viscosity ratio for this specification method. For transition modeling, Ansys states that the inlet viscosity ratio affects freestream turbulence decay and recommends, where possible, a relatively low ratio of about 1-10 with the resulting turbulence level checked near the body.
qualification: Not a NASA measurement, not inferred from NASA Tu, and not calibrated to the Run 145 thermal data. It is explicitly treated as a model input and tested at 10, 5 and 1 in the Transition SST sensitivity study.

classification: operating-point adjustment to NASA exit Mach
primary_source: Hylton et al., NASA-CR-168015 (1983), Test Conditions and Table IX; retained project development record
source_detail: NASA reports Run 145 M2 = 0.90 and states that exit-Mach levels were established by adjusting cascade exit pressure. The project initially used 241200 Pa provisionally; a second-order state at that pressure gave mass-weighted Mout = 0.88064076. A local gamma=1.4 isentropic pressure-ratio correction to Mtarget = 0.90 gave 236228.236 Pa, rounded to 236200 Pa; the continued Fluent solution then gave Mout = 0.89951531.
qualification: Not a direct NASA exit-pressure transcription. This is the documented Fluent back-pressure selection used to reproduce the experimentally controlled exit-Mach operating point. Outlet-Mach agreement is therefore an operating-point consistency check, not an independent validation metric; wall-temperature and HTC data were not used in selecting this pressure. See docs/outlet_pressure_selection.md and run145_outlet_pressure_selection.csv.
